newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat orders crackdown against corruption.
newsitem.headline: Arafat orders crackdown against corruption.

text.p: Security forces in Gaza have detained at least eight Palestinian Authority officials in a first crackdown against corruption, Attorney General Khaled al-Qidra said on Friday.
"The president (Yasser Arafat) has declared war on all aspects of corruption," Qidra said.

Members of the security forces and civilian officials holding various ranks in Arafat's self-rule administration were being questioned on charges of accepting bribes, involvement in smuggling and abuse of power, he said.
"Those officials were arrested and relentless interrogations are going on right now with them," Qidra told Reuters. He said eight people were detained.
Other private citizens were also being investigated on suspicion of smuggling Israeli goods through Jewish settlements in the Gaza Strip to Palestinian-ruled areas.
Qidra said more arrests are expected but declined to give further details.
Mohammad Dahlan, head of the Palestinian Preventive Security Service in Gaza, said Arafat had set up a committee headed by a major-general to investigate corruption.
Dahlan said investigators were compiling information on officials suspected of extortion and taking bribes and that some had already been detained.

"President Arafat has issued instructions to set up a follow-up committee and as the president said 'to strike with an iron fist against anyone, regardless of rank'," Dahlan told reporters in Gaza on Wednesday.
Charges of corruption have long plagued the Palestinian Authority, which took charge of parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip in 1994 under a self-rule deal with Israel.

In July, the Palestinian Legislative Council investigated two officials holding the rank of ministers in the Authority on suspicion of abuse of authority and laundering public funds and recommended legal action against them.
Justice Ministry officials have said that investigations were under way but no one had been charged yet.
Qidra promised the results of the investigation would be published and officials brought to trial.
